examples.trans: Nobody is here.
Please give me anything.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 됐어, 넌 무슨 죄니 중간에 껴서.
examples.trans: Forget it—what fault is it of yours, getting stuck in the middle.
Here the word for 'fault is it' is key.

examples.text: 겁도 없이 혼자 있을 때 남자 집에 들어오라고 하는 거 아니야.
examples.trans: You shouldn't fearlessly invite a man inside when you are home alone.

examples.text: 그럼 우리 일 위 후보 없이 방송 가는 거예요?
examples.trans: Then are we airing the broadcast without the first-place contender?

meanings.en: to suffer / be on the receiving end of
meanings.note: Used when someone is the victim or recipient of an undesirable event

examples.trans: My friend got hit in a fender-bender yesterday.
Be careful not to fall victim to voice phishing.

examples.text: 우리가 피디인데 애가 아무 죄 없이 당하는 거 뻔히 보면서 아무것도 못 해줘요?
examples.trans: We are her producers—how can we watch her get framed for nothing and do nothing at all?!

examples.text: 뻔히 준비하면 좋은 결과가 나올 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (plainly, right before our eyes), good results will follow.

examples.text: 뭘 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠으면 아무것도 안 하면 돼요.
examples.trans: If you don't know what to do, you don't have to do anything at all.
The topic of anything at all came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: verb to decide

examples.trans: I decided.
Let's decide.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Combines 시청 ('watching and listening') + 자 ('person').

examples.trans: Many viewers like that drama.
We listened carefully to viewer feedback.

meanings.note: Used as conditional -면 (등지면).

examples.text: 우리가 피디면 우리가 다 결정할 수 있냐? 시청자 등지면 피디가 무슨 힘이 있니?
examples.trans: Just because we are producers, do we get to decide everything? Once viewers turn their backs, what power does a producer have?
Let us do that (if we alienate) right away.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

examples.text: 잊지 않고 꼭 갚아 줄 수 있어야 피디한테 힘이 생겨.
examples.trans: Only when people know you remember and repay every debt does a producer gain power.
The topic of power, leverage came up during this shoot.
I told you last time.
What did you do last weekend?

meanings.note: 선배 + honorific suffix -님, used at work or school.

examples.trans: Senior, I have a question.
My senior said so.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.
Did you hear about this to my liking?
I was busy today because of to my liking.

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (결론을).

examples.text: 좋은 마음이 좋은 결론을 만들지는 않는다, 그거야.
examples.trans: Good intentions do not guarantee a good ending—that is what I learned.

examples.text: 누군가의 인생에 아무리 호의를 가지고 개입해도 결론이 나쁘면 그걸 누가 책임질 수 있겠냐?
examples.trans: No matter how much goodwill you bring into someone's life, if it ends badly, who can take responsibility for that?
I want to making right now.
How about trying to making together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Adverb describing acting or speaking without proper thought, caution, or respect. RR: hamburo.

examples.trans: Do not touch other people's things carelessly.
You must not make promises lightly.

meanings.note: Used as concessive -해도 (개입해도).

examples.text: 누군가의 인생에 아무리 호의를 가지고 개입해도 결론이 나쁘면 그걸 누가 책임질 수 있겠냐?
examples.trans: No matter how much goodwill you bring into someone's life, if it ends badly, who can take responsibility for that?
Let us do that (even if you step in) right away.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: Introduces a contrast, unexpected turn, or new topic. In everyday speech it is very often contracted to 근데. RR: geureonde; spoken geunde.

examples.trans: I contacted them. But there is no reply.
By the way, what time is it now?
Did you hear about this only to your side?
I was busy today because of only to your side.

examples.text: 그런데 이쪽에서 좋은 마음이었다면 비록 좋은 결론을 만들지 못했다고 해도 상대방은 알 수 있지 않을까요? 그게 큰 위로가 되지 않겠습니까?
examples.trans: Even if good intentions fail to produce a happy ending, wouldn't the other person still feel that you cared—and wouldn't that alone be a huge comfort?

examples.text: 비록 준비하면 좋은 결과가 나올 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (even though, although), good results will follow.
Did you hear about this the other person?
I was busy today because of the other person.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

examples.text: 그런데 이쪽에서 좋은 마음이었다면 비록 좋은 결론을 만들지 못했다고 해도 상대방은 알 수 있지 않을까요? 그게 큰 위로가 되지 않겠습니까?
examples.trans: Even if good intentions fail to produce a happy ending, wouldn't the other person still feel that you cared—and wouldn't that alone be a huge comfort?
The topic of comfort, consolation came up in today's meeting.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Determiner modifying a following noun.

examples.text: 그런 실수는 누구나 할 수 있어요.
examples.trans: Anyone can make a mistake like that.
This is the first time I'm hearing a story like that.

meanings.note: in expressions like 뭔 소리야? ('what are you talking about?')
audible sound made by people or things

examples.trans: Suddenly a strange sound was heard.

examples.text: 말도 안 되는 소리 하지 마.
examples.trans: Don't talk nonsense.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
